title: Oscilloscopes, analyzers and counters
blurb: Explain what scopes, spectrum analyzers, antenna analyzers and prescalers show, and how aliasing and probes affect readings.

E4A01.why: The scope only has its **samples**: the converter's **sampling rate** sets the highest frequency it can show accurately.
E4A01.trap: Q of the circuit and reference frequency don't limit the display.

E4A02.trap: Amplitude against time is an oscilloscope. SWR is an antenna analyzer's job.

E4A03.why: Spurs and IMD are extra **frequencies**, and only a **spectrum analyzer** displays signal by frequency.
E4A03.trap: A logic analyzer shows digital timing; a network analyzer measures a device's response.

E4A04.why: Display a **square wave** and trim the probe until its **flat portions are as flat as possible**.
E4A04.trap: Compensation is a square-wave test, not a sine-wave amplitude or voltage-standard adjustment.

E4A05.why: A prescaler **divides** the input down **within the counter's range**; the display restores the real value.
E4A05.trap: It divides, it doesn't multiply or amplify.

E4A06.why: Too few samples per cycle make the scope draw a **false, jittery, lower-frequency** wave: **aliasing**.
E4A06.trap: Aliasing is a sampling error, not a DC-offset or calibration fault.

E4A07.why: An antenna analyzer **computes SWR and impedance automatically**, where a bridge needs interpretation.
E4A07.trap: It measures; it doesn't tune the antenna for you.

E4A08.why: Directional wattmeter, VNA and antenna analyzer all measure SWR: **all of them**.

E4A09.why: A long ground lead adds inductance, so **keep the probe's ground connection short**.
E4A09.trap: Probes are normally high impedance and are used on both DC and AC circuits.

E4A10.why: **Line** trigger syncs the sweep to the AC line, so ripple at the line (or twice line) rate holds still.

E4A11.why: An antenna analyzer reads **velocity factor, cable length and a tuned circuit's resonant frequency**: all of them.
